Exxon also raised its quarterly dividend to $1.07 per share and plans to buy back $20 billion of its own shares in 2027.

briefs.headline: Bitcoin drops to a six-week low after a record $6.3 billion Binance hack
briefs.summary: Bitcoin fell to about $76,300 on October 30, its lowest price since mid-September and about 39% below its all-time high of $126,080. The drop came after Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange (a website where people buy and sell crypto), said hackers stole about $6.3 billion, the largest crypto theft ever. As prices fell, about $1.5 billion in borrowed-money bets on rising crypto prices were automatically closed, which pushed prices down even faster. Bitcoin is down about 7.5% over the past 30 days.
bull: About $3 billion of the stolen money has been frozen, and Binance says it will cover all customer losses with its own funds.

Some experts say the drop was mostly people who borrowed money to bet being forced out, not long-term owners selling, and one expects a bounce into the $80,000s if Bitcoin stays above $75,000 this weekend.
Bitcoin funds that trade like stocks (ETFs) still took in $17.2 million of new money on October 29.
bear: Standard Chartered, a big bank, warned prices could keep falling until more is known about the hack and the frozen money is released.
Binance found more ways the hackers got in, and has not said where the other $3.3 billion of stolen money went.
Crypto was already under pressure from high interest rates, and if Bitcoin closes below $76,600, some traders see it sliding toward $73,100.
briefs.nextEvent: Binance says it plans to restart customer withdrawals by about Nov 1, 2026, and the US midterm elections are Nov 3, 2026

briefs.summary: Ethereum (ETH) fell more than 3% to about $2,178 on October 30, its lowest price in two months, after Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange, said hackers stole about $6.3 billion. Even before the hack, Ethereum was sliding: funds that trade like stocks (ETFs) and hold Ethereum lost about $170 million over three days, and big owners sold about 160,000 ETH. About $358 million in borrowed-money bets on Ethereum were automatically closed as the price fell. Ethereum is down about 17% over the past 30 days, more than Bitcoin.
bull: Binance says user funds are safe, it will cover all losses, and about $3 billion of the stolen money has been frozen.
Some traders think that if Ethereum climbs back above $2,550, it could have room to run toward $3,000.
Ethereum ETFs have still taken in about $12.55 billion of new money in total since they started.
bear: Ethereum ETFs lost money three days in a row (Oct 26 to 28), including about $45 million from BlackRock's fund on Oct 28.
Big owners have been moving Ethereum onto exchanges, which often means they plan to sell; about 100,000 ETH arrived this week.
Standard Chartered warned crypto prices could keep falling until more is known about the hack, and some traders see $2,100 or even $2,000 as the next stop.
